 In The High Court Of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla

Versus
Shri Het Ram & Others ... Respondents.

Coram
Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ajay Mohan Goel, Judge.
Whether approved for reporting?1
_____________________________________________________
For the appellant : Mr. B.M. Chauhan, Senior Advocate,
 with Kamakshi Tarlokta, Advocate.
For the respondents : Ms. Drishti Sarswal, Advocate, vice
 Mr. Balwant Kukreja, Advocate, for
 respondent No.1.
 Mr. Tara Singh Chauhan, Senior
 Advocate, with Mr. Surya Chauhan,
 Advocate.
Ajay Mohan Goel, Judge (Oral)

By way of this appeal, the appellant/ Insurance Company has assailed Award, dated 01.01.2016,
passed by learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (Iii), Shimla, H.P., in Mac Petition No.28-S/2
of 2015/10, titled as Sh. Het Ram Versus M/s Tata Motors Ltd. & others, in terms whereof, the
Claim Petition preferred by claimant Het Ram was allowed by learned Tribunal in the following
terms:-
"36.

As a result of my findings on all the issues above, I award a sum of Rs.3,76,000/-
(Rupees three lacs and seventy six thousands only) as compensation to the petitioner
against the respondents with interest at the rate

Whether reporters of the local
papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

2024:Hhc:11655 of 7.5% per anmm from the date of petition, to the date of
realization of the entire amount.

This amount is Inclusive of any amount, if any,
awarded under Section 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Respondent Nos. 1 to 3 shall be
Decided On: 12.11.2024 vs Shri Het Ram & Others on 12 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149424329/
1
vicariously liable to pay the amount of compensation to the petitioners.

However, this
amount of compensation shall be Indemnified by respondent No. Assurance
Company Limited. prepared and file, consigned to record room."
2.

Brief facts necessary for the adjudication of the present appeal are that claimant Het Ram filed a
Claim Petition, inter alia, on the ground that on 13.02.2008, he was driving his vehicle bearing
Registration No.HP-07-4640 and he was on his way from Shimla to Parwanoo.

When the petitioner
reached near Cosmo Factory, Jabli, a Chassee being driven by Sunil Kumar (respondent No.3 in this
appeal) in a rash and negligent manner hit the vehicle of the petitioner.

On account thereof, the
petitioner sustained multiple injuries.

He was firstly taken to a Doctor at Parwanoo and thereafter,
shifted to the hospital at Chandigarh, where he remained admitted.

According to the petitioner, he
was entitled to compensation to the tune of Rs.10,00,000/- alongwith interest on account of the
accident, which took place due to rash and negligent driving of Sunil Kumar.

3. The claim was disputed by the owner of Tata Motors Limited, who denied that the Chesses was
being driven in a rash and 2024:Hhc:11655 negligent manner.

It was also denied by the owner that
any accident had taken place on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Chesses, as
was the case of the appellant.

Similarly, Driver Sunil Kumar also denied the contents of the Claim
Petition and alleged that it was the claimant who was driving the Truck in a rash and negligent
manner which led to the accident.

4. The Insurance Company took the stand that though as per the owner of the Chesses, the same was
insured with the Insurance Company, yet no details were provided by the owner of the Chesses qua
the Insurance Policy/Cover Note and the Chesses was not insured with the Insurance Company.

It
was also the stand of the Insurance Company that the accident was a result of contributory
negligence of the drivers of both the vehicles, as the vehicle were being driven in violation of the
terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.

Rest of the contents of the Claim Petition were also
denied by the Insurance Company.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, learned Tribunal framed the following issues:-
"1) Whether on 13.02.2008 near Cosmo Factory the respondent No.2 drove Chesses
in a rash and negligent manner and struck the same with the vehicle No.HP-07-
4640 being driven by the petitioner, who received multiple injuries?

Opp.
2024:Hhc:11655
2) If Issue No. 1 is proved to what amount of compensation the petitioner is entitled and from
whom?

Opp.
3) Whether the petition is not maintainable, as alleged in preliminary objection No.1?..OPR-3
Decided On: 12.11.2024 vs Shri Het Ram & Others on 12 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149424329/
2

4) Whether the petition is bad for mis-joinder and non- joinder of necessary parties as alleged in
preliminary objection No.2?
Opr-3.

5) Whether the vehicle was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the policy, as
alleged in preliminary obje
ction No.3? OPR-3 6) Whether the respondent No. 2 was not having a valid and effective driving licence at the relevant time?

OPR-3.
7) Relief."

6. On the strength of evidence which was led by the parties in support of their respective contentions, the issues so framed were answered as under:-
 "Issue No.1 : Yes  Issue No.2 : Yes  Issue No.3 : No.
 Issue No.4 : No.
 Issue No.5 : No.
 Issue No.6 : No.
 Issue No.7 : The petition is allowed per  operative portion of the award."
7.
The Claim Petition, as already mentioned hereinabove, was allowed by learned Tribunal and compensation to the tune of Rs.3,76,000/- was granted to the petitioner.
2024:HHC:11655 8. Feeling aggrieved, the Insurance Company has challenged the Award.
9. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that learned Tribunal erred in holding the Insurance Company liable to indemnify the claimant.

He submitted that as despite an application having been filed by appellant, under Order 11, Rule 12 of the Code of Civil Procedure,
the copy of the Insurance Policy was not made available to the appellant by the owner of the Chesses and as no Policy was placed on record by the owner of the Chesses, learned Tribunal gravely erred in holding the Insurance Company liable to make good the compensation amount.

Learned Senior Counsel further submitted that the driver of the Chesses in fact was not possessing a valid Driving Licence and it was indeed a fake Licence, on the basis of which, he was driving the Chesses, which was verified by the Insurance Company after the passing of the impugned Award.
Therefore also, as per him, the Award is not sustainable.

Learned Senior Counsel further submitted that even if, it is to be assumed that the Chesses was insured with the Insurance Company, yet as the Chesses was being driven in violation of the terms of the Insurance Policy, the Insurance Company could not have been fastened with the liability.
On these counts, learned Senior Counsel submitted that the impugned Award is liable to be set aside.

Learned Senior Counsel also drew the attention of the 2024:HHC:11655 Court to the application filed on behalf of the appellant, under Order 41, Rule 27 Decided On: 12.11.2024 vs Shri Het Ram & Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149424329/
3 of the Civil Procedure Code and submitted that alongwith the application, appellant has placed on record Annexure A-1, which is communication, dated 10.02.2016, addressed by the lawyer engaged by the Insurance Company, who has verified the fact that no Licence as was claimed by driver Sunil Kumar, was ever issued in his favour.
Learned Senior Counsel also referred to Annexure A-2, which as per him contains similar endorsement from the Office of Secretary, RTA, Faridabad.

10. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-claimant as well as the respondent-owner of the Chesses have strenuously argued that the findings returned by learned Tribunal in the Award under challenge are clearly borne out from the record of the case and therefore, as there is no perversity therein, the present appeal being devoid of any merit is liable to be dismissed.
They submitted that the Insurance Company miserably failed to demonstrate that the vehicle in issue was not duly insured with it or that there was any violation of the terms and conditions thereof.

They have drawn the attention of the Court to the findings returned by learned Tribunal on Issues No.5 and 6 and submitted that the findings returned qua these issues clearly demonstrate that the Insurance Company failed to prove before learned Tribunal that the Chesses was either being driven in violation of the terms and 2024:HHC:11655 conditions of the Insurance Policy or that the driver of the Chesses was not having a valid and effective Driving Licence.

11. With regard to the application filed under Order 41, Rule 27 of the Civil Procedure Code, they submitted that the documents which are now being relied upon by the appellant cannot be allowed to be taken on record, for the reason that it is not the case of the appellant that these documents were not in existence at the time when the Claim Petition was being adjudicated by learned Tribunal.

Learned counsel further submitted that the provisions of Order 41, Rule 27 of the Civil Procedure Code cannot be allowed to be used as a tool by a party to fill up the lacuna which in fact is the intent of the appellant.
Accordingly, be prayed that the present appeal being devoid of any merit be dismissed.
12. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have also carefully gone through the Award under challenge as well as the record of the case.
13. The circumstances, in which the Claim Petition was filed, have already been mentioned by me hereinabove.

The primary grounds on which the Award is being assailed by the Insurance Company is that learned Tribunal erred in not appreciating that there was no evidence from which it could be inferred that the Chesses was insured with the appellant-Insurance Company or that the Chesses was being driven by a driver who was possessing a valid 2024:HHC:11655 Driving Licence to drive the vehicle.
The Issues which were framed by learned Tribunal have already been quoted by me hereinabove.
A perusal thereof demonstrates that the onus to prove Issues No.5 and 6 was on OPR-3, i.e. the present appellant before learned Tribunal.

As it was the stand of the Insurance Company that the vehicle was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the Policy and that the driver was not possessing a valid and effective Driving Licence, the onus to prove these issues was squarely on the Insurance Company.

In fact, this Court would like to make an observation that if it was the case of the Insurance Company that there was no material on record to suggest that the Chesses was insured with the Insurance Company, then why it took the stand in the reply that the Chesses was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the Policy.
The Decided On: 12.11.2024 vs Shri Het Ram & Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149424329/

4 Court is making this observation for the reason that the Insurance Company could not have taken completely opposite stands in the reply, i.e. that on one hand that the Chesses was never insured with it and on the other hand that the same was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.

Similarly, as it was the allegation of the Insurance Company that the Chesses was being driven by a person who was not having a valid and effective Driving Licence,
the onus was upon the Insurance Company to prove the same.
A perusal of the record demonstrates that no evidence was led by the Insurance 2024:HHC:11655 Company to prove this fact before learned Tribunal.

As far as the application filed under Order 41, Rule 27 of the Civil Procedure Code is concerned, the documents which have been appended therewith, cannot be allowed to be taken on record, for the reason that there is no cogent explanation given in the application as to what prevented the Insurance Company from placing these documents on record during the course of the trial of the Claim Petition, which was not concluded by learned Tribunal in six or seven months, but was decided by learned Tribunal in about a period of six to seven years.

This clearly demonstrates that the endeavour which now is being made by the appellant is to fill up with the lacunae, which is not the intent of the provisions of Order 41, Rule 27 of the Civil Procedure Code.

Besides this, record demonstrates that there was a Cover Note (Mark-X) on record, relating to the factum of the Chesses being insured with the appellant-Insurance Company and had the appellant being diligent before learned Tribunal, then it could have taken assistance of the said Mark-X to put-forth its case in this regard.

This Court is of the considered view that as in the application filed under Order 41, Rule 27 of the Civil Procedure Code, again what is being stressed by the appellant is the fact that the driver of the Chesses was not possessing a valid Driving Licence to drive the vehicle, this again impliedly amounts to the acceptance of the fact by the Insurance Company that the Chesses indeed was 2024:HHC:11655 insured.

Had the same not been insured with the Insurance Company, as observed hereinabove also, there was no reason for the Insurance Company to have had taken the plea of the violation of the Insurance Policy.

14. In light of above observations, as this Court does not finds that there is any infirmity in the Award passed by learned Tribunal and as the same is a reasoned Award, findings whereof are clearly borne out from the pleadings and evidence on record and further, as this Court is of the considered view that the application filed under Order 41, Rule 27 of the Civil Procedure Code cannot be allowed, because no due-diligence has been demonstrated by the appellant and the intent is only to fill up the lacunae, the appeal as well as the application are dismissed.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, stand disposed of.
Interim order, if any, stands vacated.
(Ajay Mohan Goel) Judge November 12, 2024 (Rishi)
